statement: Domaine Marcel Lapierre is a family wine estate in Villié-Morgon created in 1909; its current estate page describes 18 hectares planted to Gamay noir à jus blanc, mainly in Morgon.
Domaine Marcel Lapierre states that Marcel Lapierre was born in 1950, took over the family business in 1973, and died after the 2010 harvest in October 2010.
Mathieu Lapierre joined the domaine in 2004, Camille Lapierre joined in 2013, and the siblings currently co-own and operate the family winery.

The domaine states that in 1981, under Jules Chauvet's guidance, Marcel Lapierre decided to vinify without added sulfur and shifted toward organic cultivation without chemical fertilizers or weedkillers.
Domaine Lapierre states that all plots have been worked according to organic principles since the 1980s and that the vines have been Ecocert-certified since 2004.

scope_notes: Current estate-level practice; sulfur is not universally absent.
statement: Domaine Lapierre currently describes hand harvest, semi-carbonic maceration, indigenous yeasts, used-barrel completion and aging for Morgon, no filtration, and selective sulfur use; some export batches receive a light sulfur dose while bottles marked N are bottled without sulfur.
INAO describes Morgon as a red AOP, one of the ten Beaujolais crus, with a geographic area limited to the commune of Villié-Morgon around the Py hill and production from Gamay.
Domaine Marcel Lapierre produces a recurring Morgon bottling from Gamay; CARTA treats the named bottling as one durable wine identity across vintages.
Weingut Rudi Pichler is a Wösendorf estate whose family has practiced viticulture there since 1731; the current estate states that it cultivates 15 hectares, 65% Grüner Veltliner and 30% Riesling.

Vinea Wachau records Hochrain as a terraced southeast-facing Ried at Wösendorf, 27.46 hectares in total and 215-380 metres in altitude; these are climat-wide measurements, not Rudi Pichler holding figures.
Ried Hochrain is characterized by substantial loess deposits; Vinea Wachau describes black soil over loess, while Rudi Pichler likewise identifies loess as the site's underlying material.
Weingut Rudi Pichler produces a Riesling Hochrain Smaragd, presented by the producer as a Riesling from the Wösendorf top site Hochrain.

scope_notes: Association quality category/trademark, not a government DAC tier.
statement: Smaragd is a Vinea Wachau quality category and registered trademark restricted to member wineries; Vinea currently defines Smaragd wines as at least 12.5% alcohol by volume, while Wachau DAC separately governs geographic origin.

Austria's Wachau DAC regulation §4 provides that Riedenwein bearing a Ried name must be based on Grüner Veltliner or Riesling, prohibits enrichment, requires the Ried name to be used with Wachau DAC, and requires the relevant locality name on the main label.
Aphros is a wine project led by Vasco Croft that began its modern restructuring at Casal do Paço in the Lima Valley in 2004 and later expanded to adjacent properties near Ponte de Lima.

scope_notes: Producer-described biodynamic practice; no third-party certification claim is made.
statement: Aphros describes implementing biodynamic practices beginning in the 2000s, including cover crops, animals and biodynamic preparations, and describes indigenous yeasts plus low, nonzero sulfur use in the cellar.
Aphros's current portfolio includes multiple wines under the Phaunus name, supporting treatment of Phaunus as a producer-owned wine line/project rather than a separate estate.
Aphros Wine Lda. produces Phaunus Loureiro; the 2023 first-party technical page identifies it as 100% Loureiro from Northwest Portugal.
For the 2023 Phaunus Loureiro, Aphros documents spontaneous fermentation with skins in beeswax-lined clay amphorae and seven months of sur-lies aging; the page reports total sulfur of 30 mg/L.
Aphros's project history places its foundational and expanded vineyard properties in the Lima Valley and around Ponte de Lima, with multiple Loureiro plantings on granitic sites.

resolution_needed: Confirm the legal designation printed on the relevant Phaunus Loureiro vintages before creating a WITHIN_APPELLATION edge. The current first-party Phaunus page says only Northwest Portugal, while other Aphros wines explicitly state Vinho Verde DOC / Lima.
statement: Phaunus Loureiro is securely placed in Northwest Portugal and uses Loureiro, but the current first-party Phaunus technical page does not itself state Vinho Verde DOC or Lima; CARTA therefore leaves its precise legal appellation unresolved pending label or producer confirmation.
